policy: BE source stages are manifest-defined. The base microdata is BE-SILC under Statbel/Eurostat scientific-use terms: the raw registers exist only in the licensed environment, artifacts publish to the private BE repo only (see release_contract.json), and executable Python belongs only in shared Populace runtimes.

artifacts.locator: Statbel BE-SILC scientific-use files: D (household register), R (personal register), H (household data), P (personal data)
artifacts.licence: Statbel/Eurostat scientific-use; restricted — private artifacts only

operations.notes: EU-SILC register linkage: personal ids embed the household id (RB030 carries DB030 plus the person sequence); the shared runtime owns the arithmetic.

SILC survey year N carries year N-1 incomes. The build's period bookkeeping and every target profile bind to the income reference year through this declaration; see PolicyEngine/ledger#71 for the facts-vs-projections basis this feeds.

EU-SILC names to frame/engine names. PY010G (gross employee cash or near-cash income) feeds the Axiom CIR 1992 article 23 worker-remuneration input; further income and contribution inputs join this mapping as the encoded slice grows.
Age at the end of the income reference year.
Frame membership column per the kernel linkage convention.

stages.notes: The base population stage (populace#262 owns the runtime). Entity posture per the adapter (populace#260): person plus household; Belgian PIT is individual with household-level elements, so no separate fiscal unit enters until the encoded slice needs one.
